Apply to join us at the School of Science
If you’re ready to be challenged, to dive in deep to scientific topics, and to grow in ways you never thought possible, you’re ready to apply to become a School of Science student.
You’ll start the admissions process by completing the IU Indianapolis online application for your academic level.

How to apply for undergraduate admission to the School of Science
There are two ways to become a student in the School of Science.
Direct admission as a beginning or transfer student
Admission through University College after completing requirements
To be considered for direct admission, indicate your interest in one of our majors on the online application. We will automatically consider you for direct admit status if you meet the requirements.
Freshman and transfer students who are not eligible for direct admission to the School of Science will be admitted to the IU Indianapolis University College STEM cluster as pre-science students. You will complete the same course of study as directly admitted students. Once you have completed the requirements you can apply to the School of Science as an internal applicant.
Medicine and dentistry pathway programs
In connection with the IU School of Medicine and the IU School of Dentistry, the IU Indianapolis School of Science provides conditional admission to the School of Medicine or School of Dentistry for qualified beginning freshmen who are directly admitted to the School of Science.
Learn more about these programs and how to apply »

Direct admission requirements
Direct admission requirements for beginning students
There are two paths to direct admission for incoming high school students:
You have a high school GPA of 3.3 and can provide evidence of readiness for the first math course in your respective major
You have a high school GPA of 3.0 with minimum SAT scores of 1080 (530 math) OR minimum ACT scores of 21 composite and 21 math.*
*Physics applicants need minimum or comparable SAT scores of 570 math and a combined reading/math score of 1110.
Math requirements by degree
Psychology B.A. and B.S.—Evidence of readiness for M118 Finite or MATH-I 153 College Algebra by completing Algebra 2 in the final year of high school.
Biology B.A., Geology B.A.—Evidence of readiness for MATH-I 153 College Algebra by completing Algebra 2 in the final year of high school.
Environmental Science B.S.—Evidence of readiness for MATH-I 231 Calculus for Life Sciences I by completing Pre-Calculus or Trigonometry in the final year of high school.
Biology B.S., Neuroscience B.S.—Evidence of readiness for MATH-I 231 Calculus for Life Sciences I by completing Pre-Calculus or Trigonometry in the final year of high school.
All other degrees—Evidence of readiness for MATH-I 165 Analytic Geometry and Calculus I by completing Pre-Calculus or Trigonometry in the final year of high school.
Note: The suggested class is a minimum; any course higher than what is indicated would be acceptable.
Direct admission requirements for transfer and current IU Indianapolis students
Completion of an introductory science course or mathematics course will qualify a transfer student or current IU Indianapolis student for admission into any of our science majors.
Acceptable courses include those that have been evaluated to be equivalent to the corresponding IU Indianapolis course or have been completed at IU Indianapolis:
BIOL-K101
BIOL-K103
CHEM-C105
CHEM-C106
GEOL-G107
GEOL-G110
MATH-I 165 (or equivalent calculus course or above)
PHYS-P201
PHYS-P202
PHYS-I 152
PHYS-I 251
Applicants must have a C+ or better in one course or a C or better in two courses.
All neuroscience, environmental science, and geology transfers will be directly admitted to the School of Science.
For pre-neuroscience majors in university college, NSCI-B201 would also be acceptable for admission.
For psychology majors, in addition to the list of courses above, PSY-B110 is also acceptable for admission.
Admission as a current IU Indianapolis student
Whether you’re a current University College student or are part of another school on campus, you’ll need to apply to the School of Science before you can declare a science major. To be eligible, you must have a minimum GPA of 2.0.
The process is simple:
Review the requirements in the Direct admission requirements for transfer and current IU Indianapolis students section (above)
Complete the internal application
A decision will be emailed to you within four to six weeks. Please contact Darryl Newsom at danewsom@iu.edu if you have any questions.
Special note for graduate students
While completing the online IU Indianapolis graduate application is the first step, each department has its own admissions criteria and procedures. Please make sure you follow their guidelines.
